title: You keep hiding it…
paragraphs:
You keep hiding it…
but God already saw it.
And that’s exactly why this will shake you.

Because the thing you’re most ashamed of…
is not the thing that disqualified you.
It’s the place where grace is about to hit you hardest.

You smile in public.
You lift your hands in worship.
You say “I’m okay.”

You replay that moment.
That failure.
That secret you swore no one would ever know.

“God chose others… not you.”
“You had your chance.”
“You ruined it.”
It tells you to hide like Adam in the garden.

After sin entered, Adam didn’t run to God.
He ran from Him.
“I was afraid… so I hid.” — Genesis 3:10
It makes you cover what God is trying to heal.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.

Still coming to church…
but hiding.

Still believing…
but quietly disqualified in your own mind.
Because your story didn’t start with your sin.
“You did not choose Me, but I chose you…” — John 15:16
God didn’t choose a future version of you.

He chose you fully aware of what you would struggle with.
Fully aware of your weakness.
Fully aware of your breaking points.
Some scholars interpret this verse as referring specifically to the disciples’ calling.
But the principle reveals something deeper about the heart of Christ:
Because this is where many people twist grace.

They hear “God chose me,”
and they think,

Sin still destroys.
Sin still separates.
Sin still costs.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

Not self-help.
Not behavior modification.
Not “try harder next time.”

You are more sinful than you want to admit…
and more loved than you ever imagined.
Because God didn’t ignore your sin.
Jesus didn’t die for a cleaned-up version of you.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

While you were still in it.
Not after.
Not when you improved.
Not when you became “worthy.”
In the middle of your mess.
And this is where shame loses its power.
“I do not know the man!” — Matthew 26:74
That’s the kind of failure people don’t recover from.
This is the pattern of grace.

Sin exposed.
Heart broken.
Grace offered.
Life restored.
If God chose you knowing your worst moments…
Then your worst moments cannot cancel His calling.
But this is your moment now.
Or will you come into the light?
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
You don’t need to clean yourself first.
Because Jesus is not waiting to condemn you.
Say it if you mean it:

“Jesus… I’ve been hiding.
But I’m coming back.”

Shame breaks.
Grace floods.
Identity is restored.
If this stirred something deep in you…
